meta.title: Buka Robots
meta.description: Adds a Robots page to the sidebar. A robot is a directory the plugin creates under ~/.cache/dsh-plugin-robots/robots and mounts as a DSH workspace; only robots created here are managed. For each robot you can install project-level skills through npx skills, edit its AGENTS.md, open its conversation, or re-mount it after the workspace was removed. Every robot also has a preset avatar (assigned on creation, changeable from the page), and the plugin exposes the ctx.bukaRobots service (list, avatarMap, a blocking startSession and non-blocking dispatchSession / openSession with an observable handle; every robot session submits a structured JSON result through a scoped structured_output tool, optionally constrained by outputSchema and workflow route names, with bounded result retries and an optional abortable escape for workflow nodes, and runs as a normal runtime-root conversation under the normal approval policy, so it can request tool approvals or ask the user) for other plugins such as Buka Workflows. Installing the plugin also adds the robot-builder mode: new sessions can pick 机器人构建, which asks what the robot should do, drafts its AGENTS.md, then creates and mounts the robot with the preset-only buka_robot_build tool; creating, editing and skill installation on the page keep working. A general-purpose robot sits at the top of the list (fixed 🤖 avatar, standard mode, enters any existing workspace); a toggle in the page's Settings dialog, persisted in settings.json, decides whether it is shown. Every robot also carries a one-sentence responsibility statement (like a skill description) returned by the read-only buka_robots tool, so a workflow orchestrator can decide whether to use it. While enabled, the general-purpose robot also appears at the end of that list with the same fields as any other robot; disabling it hides it from the page and from workflows. Every robot can be renamed: the robot directory is moved to the new name, its registry entry is updated and its DSH workspace is re-registered at the new path, and earlier conversations are kept in history but no longer listed under the robot.
